title: vLLM NemotronVL/KimiK25 -- T1195.002 hardcoded trust_remote_code bypasses the operator's own flag
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-4944 (CVSS 8.8 HIGH), affecting
vllm-project/vllm 0.14.1.

Two model implementation files --
`vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_vl.py` and
`vllm/model_executor/models/kimi_k25.py` -- hardcode
`trust_remote_code=True` internally, silently overriding an operator's
explicit `--trust-remote-code=False` startup flag. Since
`trust_remote_code` controls whether HuggingFace Hub model repositories
are allowed to ship and execute their own custom Python code alongside
weights, this hardcoding means an operator who believes they have
disabled arbitrary-code-execution-on-load is still exposed the moment a
NemotronVL or KimiK25 model is loaded -- a malicious HuggingFace
repository masquerading as either architecture achieves RCE regardless
of the operator's own configuration. The advisory notes this is an
INCOMPLETE fix for two PRIOR CVEs (CVE-2025-66448, CVE-2026-22807) --
those closed other code paths, but these two model files were missed.

Detection logic flags a model-load event whose model architecture
matches NemotronVL or KimiK25 on a vLLM instance that was started with
`--trust-remote-code=False` (or the flag omitted, since `False` is the
default) -- the exact configuration the operator believed protected
them.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor bounty disclosure (huntr.com,
cross-referencing vllm-project's own two prior CVEs this one is an
incomplete fix for).
